facts.fact: The World Bank Program Paper proposes US$69m additional financing, including US$750,000 for EMIS enhancement, to integrate all 57 refugee primary schools, which currently operate outside the Ministry of Education's EMIS, and their learners into the national EMIS.

HISP Ethiopia and the HISP Centre report that from November 2025 a UNICEF-backed project in the SER, SWEPR, Oromia and Benishangul Gumuz regions works to connect local school, woreda and zone data systems to the Ministry's national DHIS2-Ed EMIS enterprise application.

systems.owner: Ministry of Education, EMIS and ICT Executive Office

note: The foreword says only that the EMIS collects and processes education data at decentralised levels; no link between systems is stated.

facts.fact: The World Bank deal record for ETOL additional financing (wb-eth-004) states the grants integrate all 57 refugee primary schools and their learners into the national EMIS, with US$750,000 earmarked for EMIS enhancement and disaggregated reporting, the schools currently being outside the Ministry's EMIS.

note: Document states only an e-invoice system launched for the Ministry of Revenues; no fact the study asks.
Only a general aim to connect data; no link between named education systems is stated.
